questions.questionHtml:
⚡ GO Classes CS 2027 Style | Linked Lists

Floyd's Cycle-Finding Algorithm (tortoise and hare) uses two pointers moving at speeds 1 and 2 respectively. If a linked list has a non-cyclic prefix of length $\mu$ and a cycle of length $\lambda$, where do the two pointers first meet relative to the start of the cycle?

💡 Official Solution & Step-by-Step Derivation:
When the slow pointer enters the cycle at step $\mu$, the fast pointer is at position $(2\mu - \mu) \pmod \lambda = \mu \pmod \lambda$. The distance fast must catch up is $\lambda - (\mu \pmod \lambda)$. With relative speed 1 step/iteration, they meet at distance $(\lambda - (\mu \pmod \lambda)) \pmod \lambda$.
